contents.html: This is the report of the Invitational Workshop on Public Key Infrastructure, which was jointly sponsored by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), the Security Infrastructure Program Management Office (SI-PMO) and the MITRE Corporation. A public key infrastructure provides a means for issuing and managing public key certificates, which may be used to provide security services, such as authentication, integrity, confidentiality and non-repudiation, between strangers who have no previous knowledge of each other. Papers were presented on the current state of technology and standards for a Public Key Infrastructure, management and technical issues, escrowing keys used for confidentiality exchanges, and cost models.
contents.html_ja: 本書は、国立標準技術研究所（NIST）、セキュリティ基盤プログラム管理室（SI-PMO）、MITRE Corporation が共同で後援した公開鍵基盤に関する招待ワークショップの報告書です。公開鍵基盤は、公開鍵証明書を発行・管理する手段を提供します。公開鍵証明書は、互いについての事前の知識を持たない他人同士の間で、認証、完全性、機密性、否認防止などのセキュリティサービスを提供するために使用できます。ワークショップでは、公開鍵基盤の技術と標準の現状、管理上および技術上の課題、機密性の交換に使用する鍵の預託、およびコストモデルについての論文が発表されました。

contents.html: Robert Rosenthal, Co-Chair, NIST
contents.html_ja: Robert Rosenthal、共同議長、NIST
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p9: 太字の署名見出し

contents.html: Many government and industry organizations recognize the need for privacy and security in the National Information Infrastructure or NII. Important applications in business, medicine and other areas are likely to use public key cryptography and digital signature mechanisms to provide integrity, authentication, nonrepudiation and confidentiality key management security services. These powerful security techniques, when provided on a large national or worldwide basis, will enable secure transactions among partners who may never meet each other personally, where their transactions may be exposed to unknown parties and where untrusted communications and storage systems may be prevalent. The opportunity exists now to develop a ubiquitous, interoperable Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) meeting the widest spectrum of government, industry, and personal needs.
contents.html_ja: 政府および産業界の多くの組織が、国家情報基盤（NII）におけるプライバシーとセキュリティの必要性を認識しています。ビジネス、医療などの重要なアプリケーションでは、完全性、認証、否認防止、および機密性のための鍵管理というセキュリティサービスを提供するために、公開鍵暗号とデジタル署名の仕組みが使用される可能性が高いです。これらの強力なセキュリティ技術が国全体または世界規模で提供されれば、互いに直接会うことがないかもしれない相手同士が、取引を未知の第三者にさらしうる状況や、信頼できない通信・記憶システムが広く存在しうる状況で、安全に取引を行えるようになります。政府、産業界、個人の最も幅広いニーズを満たす、どこでも使える相互運用可能な公開鍵基盤（PKI）を開発する機会が、今まさにあります。
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p9: 画像と語ごとに照合。OCR の "NIL" を "NII." に直す
contents.translation_resolve_note: 旧訳は鍵管理を全サービスに係らせていた。confidentiality key management は機密性のための鍵管理（鍵配送）と読み、英文の語順どおりに直す。

contents.html: The federal government has begun work on the design of a Public Key Infrastructure to support the management of the public key certificates and keys it needs. Guidance for this work comes from many sources including our own internal research projects, cooperative programs with industry, other federal agencies, and, interactions in open forums like this invitational workshop. At NIST, we actively solicit inputs from designers and users alike to mold and formulate the ideas that drive our government programs in this area.
contents.html_ja: 連邦政府は、必要とする公開鍵証明書と鍵の管理を支援する公開鍵基盤の設計に着手しました。この作業の指針は、NIST 自身の内部研究プロジェクト、産業界や他の連邦機関との協力プログラム、そして今回の招待ワークショップのような公開フォーラムでの交流など、多くの情報源から得られています。NIST では、この分野の政府プログラムを推進する考え方を形づくり、まとめるために、設計者と利用者の双方からの意見を積極的に求めています。

contents.html_ja: このワークショップの計画、実施、参加にあたり、MITRE Corporation および一般調達局（General Services Administration）と協力できたことを喜ばしく思います。議論から明らかになったのは、この変化の激しい分野において、参加者が協力し情報を共有する必要性と意欲があることでした。
contents.html: We are pleased to have worked with the MITRE Corporation and the General Services Administration to plan, execute and participate in this workshop. A clear result of the discussions was the need for and willingness of the participants to cooperate and share information in this dynamic area.

contents.html: Richard J. Kemp, Co-Chair, SI-PMO
contents.html_ja: Richard J. Kemp、共同議長、SI-PMO
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p9: 太字の署名見出しと段落を分ける（画像と語ごとに照合）

contents.html_ja: 政府の電子的な業務が成り立つには、セキュリティサービスが必要です。従来のデータセキュリティモデルでは、エンドユーザーとそのアプリケーションに対して、認証、アクセス制御、データの完全性、否認防止、機密性という 5 つの基本的なセキュリティサービスが提供されます。現実には、これらのサービスは、公開鍵基盤がなければ、相互接続された世界（私たちが向かいつつある世界）では提供できません。PKI は、ビジネス目標を安全に達成するための不可欠な実現技術です。
contents.html: The electronic business of Government requires security services to be viable. In the traditional data security model, there are five basic security services offered to end users and their applications: Authentication, Access Control, Data Integrity, Non-Repudiation, and Confidentiality. As a practical matter, these services cannot be delivered in an internetworked world (the one we are moving towards) without a Public Key Infrastructure. PKI is the essential enabling technology for accomplishing business objectives in a secure fashion.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p9: 太字の署名見出しと段落を分ける（画像と語ごとに照合）

contents.html: The purpose of the Federal Information Security Infrastructure Program Management Office (SI-PMO) is to provide government wide support and coordination of Federal activities necessary to implement an information security infrastructure for the use of the Federal Government. Since the private sector will lead in the development and implementation of end application security solutions, the SI-PMO will, in coordination with NIST, interact directly and continuously with private industry. The SI-PMO must articulate the needs of the federal government as a customer community, and also understand the commercial offerings, and how commercially available information security solutions can be applied to solving the government's problems.
contents.html_ja: 連邦情報セキュリティ基盤プログラム管理室（SI-PMO）の目的は、連邦政府が使用する情報セキュリティ基盤を実装するために必要な連邦の活動について、政府全体の支援と調整を行うことです。エンドアプリケーションのセキュリティソリューションの開発と実装は民間部門が主導するため、SI-PMO は NIST と調整しながら、民間企業と直接かつ継続的に交流します。SI-PMO は、顧客コミュニティとしての連邦政府のニーズを明確に示すとともに、市販の製品を理解し、市販の情報セキュリティソリューションを政府の問題の解決にどう適用できるかも理解しなければなりません。

contents.html: Public forums and workshops such as this one, serve to ensure the interchange of information most necessary for the effective development and implementation of the security infrastructure. We look forward to continued joint efforts with NIST, the MITRE Corporation, and other activities to share information and experiences in this vital evolving technical area
contents.html_ja: 本ワークショップのような公開フォーラムや会合は、セキュリティ基盤を効果的に開発・実装するために最も必要な情報交換を確かなものにする役割を果たします。この重要で発展中の技術分野で情報と経験を共有するために、NIST、MITRE Corporation、その他の活動との共同の取り組みが今後も続くことを期待しています。

U.S. DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE Technology Administration National Institute of Standards and Technology Computer Security Division Information Technology Laboratory Gaithersburg, MD 20899
Sponsored by: National Institue of Standards and Technology MITRE Corporation Federal Information Security Infrastructure Program Management Office
Invitational September 28, 1995 MITRE Corporation McLean, Virginia
U.S. DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE Technology Administration National Institute of Standards and Technology Computer Security Division Information Technology Laboratory Gaithersburg, MD 20899
Sponsored by: National Institue of Standards and Technology MITRE Corporation Federal Information Security Infrastructure Program Management Office
U.S. DEPARTMENT OF COMMERCE Ronald H. Brown, Secretary TECHNOLOGY ADMINISTRATION Mary L. Good, Under Secretary for Technology NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF STANDARDS AND TECHNOLOGY Arati Prabhakar, Director

This is the report of the Invitational Workshop on Public Key Infrastructure, which was jointly sponsored by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), the Security Infrastructure Program Management Office (SI-PMO) and the MITRE

Corporation. public key infrastructure provides a means for issuing and managing public key certificates, which may be used to provide security services, such as authentication, integrity, confidentiality and non-repudiation, between strangers who have no previous knowledge of each other. Papers were presented on the current state of technology and standards for a Public Key Infrastructure, management and technical issues, escrowing keys used for confidentiality exchanges, and cost models.

The views expressed by the participants of this workshop are their own and do not necessarily reflect those of the sponsoring organizations. Proprietary names and model numbers are cited for clarity and do not imply recommendation or endorsement by the sponsors.

Many government and industry organizations recognize the need for privacy and security in the National Information Infrastructure or NIL Important applications in business, medicine and other areas are likely to use public key cryptography and digital signature mechanisms to provide integrity, authentication, nonrepudiation and confidentiality key management security services. These powerful security techniques, when provided on a large national or worldwide basis, will enable secure transactions among partners who may never meet each other personally, where their transactions may be exposed to unknown parties and where untrusted communications and storage systems may be prevalent. The opportunity exists now to develop a ubiquitous, interoperable Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) meeting the widest spectrum of government, industry, and personal needs.

The federal government has begun work on the design of a Public Key Infrastructure to support the management of the public key certificates and keys it needs. Guidance for this work comes from many sources including our own internal research projects, cooperative programs with industry, other federal agencies, and, interactions in open forums like this invitational workshop. At NIST, we actively solicit inputs from designers and users alike to mold and formulate the ideas that drive our government programs in this area. We are pleased to have worked with the MITRE Corporation and the General Services

Administration to plan, execute and participate in this workshop. clear result of the discussions was the need for and willingness of the participants to cooperate and share information in this dynamic area.

Richard J. Kemp, Co-Chair, SI-PMO The electronic business of Government requires security services to be viable. In the traditional data security model, there are five basic security services offered to end users and their applications: Authentication, Access Control, Data Integrity, Non-Repudiation, and Confidentiality. As a practical matter, these services cannot be delivered in an internetworked world (the one we are moving towards) without a Public Key Infrastructure. PKI is the essential enabling technology for accomplishing business objectives in a secure fashion.

The purpose of the Federal Information Security Infrastructure Program Management Office (SI-PMO) is to provide government wide support and coordination of Federal activities necessary to implement an information security infrastructure for the use of the Federal Government. Since the private sector will lead in the development and implementation of end application security solutions, the SI-PMO will, in coordination with NIST, interact directly and continuously with private industry. The SI-PMO must articulate the needs of the federal government as a customer community, and also understand the commercial offerings, and how commercially available information security solutions can be applied to solving the government's problems.
Public forums and workshops such as this one, serve to ensure the interchange of information most necessary for the effective development and implementation of the
security infrastructure. look forward to continued joint efforts with NIST, the MITRE Corporation, and other activities to share information and experiences in this vital evolving technical area
